title: Split Conformal Risk Control — Mathematical Reconciliation Audit
inf_sup_equivalence_note: ADR 004 formulation inf{lam : (n/(n+1)) R_n(lam) + 1/(n+1) <= alpha} can be read two ways. For the loss L = I(Y=1 AND S<lam), R_n(lam) is NON-DECREASING in lam (higher threshold means more false negatives). The safe set S_safe = { lam : bound(lam) <= alpha } is therefore a closed interval [0, lam*]. The SUPREMUM of this interval (lam*) is the most aggressive (largest) threshold satisfying the bound -- used in the patent claim. The ADR 004 inf{} notation is the infimum of the COMPLEMENT (unsafe) set, which equals the supremum of the safe set. Both produce the identical operational threshold lam*. The patent specification (Claim 2) correctly uses sup{} and is consistent with the implementation.

patent_claim_reconciliation.claim_2_sup_formulation: CORRECT — sup{safe set} equals inf{complement set} for monotone loss.
patent_claim_reconciliation.claim_3_fnr_5pct: The 5% risk bound is computed with n_positive denominator (conditional FNR) as implemented in ADR 004. This is the conditional false-negative rate E[I(C_λ=0) | Y=1]. The Bates et al. (2021) theorem bounds the unconditional risk E[L(X,Y)] = P(Y=1) * conditional_FNR. The specification Section 7.4 has been updated to make this distinction explicit.
patent_claim_reconciliation.claim_recommended_language: ...wherein the empirical risk R_n(λ) is defined as the conditional false-negative rate among positive calibration studies: R_n(λ) = (1/n_pos) Σ_{i: Y_i=1} I(S(X_i) < λ), with the bound selected as λ = sup{ λ' : (n/(n+1)) R_n(λ') + 1/(n+1) ≤ α }.

pointing_game_e2_clarification.evidence: step11b_hirescam_pointing.py iterates `for _, bbox_row in study_df.iterrows()`, incrementing study_total += 1 per bbox_row (i.e., per bounding box). n_total_bboxes=6283, n_hits=2754, hit_rate=43.83% are box-level metrics. The patent specification should state: 'pointing-game hit rate of 43.83% evaluated per expert bounding box annotation (n=6,283 boxes across 226 studies).'

claim_9_monotonicity_clarification.non_monotone_at: sigma=0.35 (variance drops from 0.00496 at sigma=0.20 to 0.00409)
claim_9_monotonicity_clarification.recommendation: Claim 9 should be weakened. Replace 'monotonic non-decreasing rank correlation (Spearman rho >= 0.85)' with 'positive rank correlation (Spearman rho > 0) across discrete image acquisition noise levels, as evaluated experimentally.' The specification Section 7.6 already correctly states the exact rho=0.9000 over 5 discrete levels, which is sufficient technical disclosure.
